steps.message:
In `rich/live.py`, `Live.stop()` does:

```python
    def stop(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Stop live rendering display.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            if not self._started:\n                return\n            self._started = False
```

So if `Progress.start()` was not called (because `self.disable` is True), `self.live._started` will be False, and `self.live.stop()` will return immediately without doing anything.

The bug was that `Progress.stop()` would print a blank line on non-interactive consoles even when the `Progress` object was initialized with `disabled=True`. I fixed this by wrapping the contents of the `stop()` method in `rich/progress.py` within an `if not self.disable:` block, making it symmetric to the `start()` method. This ensures that no output is generated when the progress display is disabled.
